title: Buyers vs Sellers
hook: Price moves based on who's stronger. Read it like a story, not a guess.
mission: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to point to the exact moment control changed hands in a series of candles.

blocks.heading: Price moves because buyers and sellers are fighting for control

beats.heading: Who's winning right now
beats.body: Buyers think price should go higher. Sellers think price should go lower. When buyers are stronger, price lifts. When sellers are stronger, price drops.

beats.heading: The body matters more than the drama
beats.body: Long wicks can look dramatic, but the body tells you where price actually settled. Later in ICC, close beats wick.

blocks.heading: Find where control changed
blocks.prompt: This price path steps higher with a couple of small pullbacks, then something changes. Tap the point where sellers actually took control.

points.feedback: That's a small pullback inside an uptrend that's still holding — not a real change of control.
Exactly. That's the point where price actually closed lower and broke the pattern — a real shift, not just a wick.
Another shallow pullback — buyers were still winning through this point.

blocks.quote: The body matters more than the drama. Long wicks can look dramatic, but the body tells you where price actually settled — later in ICC, close beats wick.

questions.question: A string of strong green closes with small pullbacks usually means:
questions.why: Repeated strong closes with shallow pullbacks is buyers repeatedly winning the disagreement.

questions.question: A candle wicks below a key higher low intraday but closes back above it by the end of the period. Did sellers take control of that candle?
options: No — the close shows buyers reclaimed it before the period ended
Yes — any wick below a level means sellers won
It depends only on the candle's color
questions.why: The close is what decides who actually won that candle; the wick just shows how far the fight went.

blocks.prompt: Imagine another AGHF girl asks: "How do you tell who's winning on a chart?" How would you explain it to her, in your own words?

takeaways: Buyers push price up, sellers push price down — candles show who won each round.
A wick shows a fight happened; the close shows who actually won it.
Control can shift mid-story — keep reading, don't assume it stays the same.
remember: The close is the scoreboard. The wick is just the fight.
